status: SEED - validated against the 5 demo scenarios by the test suite

evaluation.order: ascending priority; the FIRST rule whose predicates all match wins
predicate_vocabulary: any  - value contains at least one of the given substrings (case-insensitive)
none - value contains none of the given substrings
all  - value contains every one of the given substrings
eq / not_eq - equality against a scalar
lt / lte / gt / gte - numeric comparison
exists - the field is present and not empty
evaluation.default_rationale: No emergency or urgent indicator was found in the reported symptoms.

clinical_notes: RED = emergency, needs hospital now. YELLOW = urgent, needs same-day clinic care.
GREEN = routine, can be managed at home or at a routine clinic visit.
Rules are ordered so that no YELLOW can ever be shadowed by a GREEN rule.
This engine is deliberately deterministic: an LLM extraction failure can make a result more cautious, never less. See backend/triage/engine.py.
Clinical review by a licensed Kenyan clinician is still PENDING (see PILOT_TODO).

rules.name: Cardiac emergency - chest pain with breathing difficulty
rules.rationale: Chest pain together with difficulty breathing may be a heart attack. This cannot be excluded at primary care level.

rules.name: Cardiac emergency - chest pain with cardiac red flags
rules.rationale: Chest pain with cardiac features (radiation, sweating, fainting, palpitations) is treated as a heart attack until proven otherwise.

rules.name: Malaria danger sign - fever with neurological or respiratory compromise
rules.rationale: Fever with confusion, convulsions, inability to drink or laboured breathing suggests severe malaria or another life-threatening infection.

rules.name: Severe respiratory distress
rules.rationale: Severe difficulty breathing, chest indrawing or inability to speak in full sentences is respiratory failure until proven otherwise.

rules.name: Neurological emergency
rules.rationale: Loss of consciousness, convulsions or new weakness on one side of the body requires immediate hospital assessment.

rules.name: Mental health emergency - suicidal ideation
rules.rationale: Thoughts of self-harm or suicide require immediate mental health intervention. Do not leave the patient alone.

rules.name: Obstetric emergency - bleeding in pregnancy
rules.rationale: Vaginal bleeding in pregnancy is an obstetric emergency - possible miscarriage, ectopic pregnancy or placenta praevia.

rules.name: Diabetic emergency
rules.rationale: Fruity-smelling breath, deep rapid breathing, drowsiness or a foot ulcer in a person with diabetes suggests ketoacidosis or severe complication.

rules.name: High fever with respiratory symptoms
rules.rationale: High fever together with a cough or breathing symptoms suggests pneumonia, severe malaria or tuberculosis. Needs clinical examination today.

rules.name: Febrile illness - malaria or typhoid must be excluded
rules.rationale: Fever with headache, chills, body aches or nausea is a febrile illness. In Kenya malaria and typhoid must be excluded with a test - this needs a same-day clinic visit.

rules.name: Severe febrile illness without focal symptoms
rules.rationale: A high fever on its own is an urgent presentation in a malaria-endemic setting and needs same-day assessment.

rules.name: Fever with focal urinary symptoms
rules.rationale: Fever with burning or frequent urination, or fever with back pain, suggests kidney involvement (pyelonephritis) rather than simple cystitis.

rules.name: Dehydration from vomiting or diarrhoea
rules.rationale: Diarrhoea or vomiting with signs of dehydration or blood in the stool requires rehydration and assessment today.

rules.name: Mental health crisis - functional collapse without suicidal ideation
rules.rationale: Severe depression or anxiety that prevents the patient from functioning at work, school or home needs same-day mental health assessment. Mental health care is covered under SHA without a referral.

rules.name: Chest pain without cardiac features
rules.rationale: Chest pain that does not match an emergency pattern still needs a same-day ECG-capable assessment. It is not managed at home.

rules.name: Suspected tuberculosis - cough lasting over two weeks
rules.rationale: A cough lasting more than two weeks requires tuberculosis screening, with or without fever.

rules.name: Hypertensive urgency
rules.rationale: A blood pressure reading at or above 180/110 mmHg, or severe headache with blurred vision in a person with hypertension, needs same-day assessment to prevent stroke.

rules.name: Spreading skin infection
rules.rationale: Red streaks spreading up a limb, fever with a skin infection, or rapidly spreading redness suggests cellulitis requiring systemic antibiotics.

rules.name: Significant injury needing clinical care
rules.rationale: A deep wound, bleeding that is hard to stop, a suspected fracture or a wound from a dirty object needs wound care, suturing or tetanus vaccination today.

rules.name: Uncomplicated upper respiratory infection
rules.rationale: A runny nose, sore throat or mild cough with no high fever or breathing difficulty is usually self-limiting and can be managed at home.

rules.name: Mild fever without danger signs
rules.rationale: Mild fever in a patient who is drinking, alert and playing is usually a self-limiting viral illness. Review if it persists beyond three days.

rules.name: Mild diarrhoea without dehydration
rules.rationale: Simple diarrhoea without dehydration signs is managed at home with oral rehydration solution and fluids.

rules.name: Routine chronic disease follow-up
rules.rationale: A scheduled review of controlled hypertension or diabetes with no new symptoms is routine. Continue treatment and keep the appointment.

rules.name: Localised skin infection
rules.rationale: A small, localised, non-spreading skin infection can be managed with wound care and topical treatment.

rules.name: Minor injury
rules.rationale: A minor cut, bruise or graze can be cleaned and dressed at home. Attend a clinic if it shows signs of infection.

rules.name: Default routine care
rules.rationale: No emergency or urgent indicator was identified from the reported symptoms. A routine clinic visit is appropriate if symptoms continue.
